entities.name: Donatus of Arezzo
entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Saint Donatus of Arezzo is the patron saint of Arezzo and a bishop of the city. Born around 300 AD, his life was marked by controversy and opposition from rival factions. Despite these challenges, he worked tirelessly to promote Christianity throughout the region. The church he founded in Arezzo became a major pilgrimage site during the Middle Ages, attracting visitors from across Europe. Donatus's legacy extends beyond his own city, influencing the development of Christian theology and practices in Italy and surrounding regions. "We must obey God rather than men," he famously said, in his treatise on the nature of salvation. This enigmatic phrase has been interpreted as a call to resist oppressive authority and instead follow one's conscience. As such, Donatus remains an important figure in Italian history, symbolizing the struggles and triumphs of early Christian communities.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Donatus of Arezzo played a significant role in the development of Christianity in Italy, promoting Trinitarian theology and practices throughout the region.
